model_annotations.Bulgarian: This bar chart illustrates the relationship between sparsity rate and perplexity for two different pruning strategies: “Per-Output” (blue bars) and “Per-Layer” (orange bars), with perplexity plotted on a logarithmic y-axis ranging from 10¹ to 10³ and sparsity rates on the x-axis ranging from 10% to 80% in 10% increments. At lower sparsity rates (10%–50%), both methods exhibit similarly low perplexity values, hovering just above 10¹. As sparsity increases beyond 50%, perplexity rises sharply for both methods, with the “Per-Layer” strategy consistently showing higher perplexity than “Per-Output” at each sparsity level. At 80% sparsity, the “Per-Output” method reaches a perplexity of approximately 500, while “Per-Layer” exceeds 1000, indicating a more severe degradation in model performance under aggressive layer-wise pruning. The chart visually emphasizes the trade-off between model compression (sparsity) and language modeling quality (perplexity), with “Per-Output” pruning demonstrating greater robustness to high sparsity.
model_annotations.Chinese: This bar chart illustrates the relationship between sparsity rate and perplexity for two different pruning strategies—“Per-Output” (blue) and “Per-Layer” (orange)—across sparsity rates ranging from 10% to 80%. The vertical axis, labeled “Perplexity,” is displayed on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10¹ to 10³, with major gridlines at 10, 100, and 1000. The horizontal axis, labeled “Sparsity Rate,” shows discrete categories at 10% intervals. For each sparsity rate, two adjacent bars represent the respective perplexity values of the two methods. At low sparsity (10%–40%), both methods yield nearly identical and very low perplexity (around 5–7). As sparsity increases, perplexity rises for both, with “Per-Layer” consistently showing slightly higher perplexity than “Per-Output” at each level. At 80% sparsity, “Per-Output” reaches a perplexity of approximately 500, while “Per-Layer” exceeds 1000, indicating a more severe degradation in performance under aggressive pruning. The chart visually emphasizes the growing divergence in model quality between the two pruning approaches as sparsity increases.
